minors.title: Unreachable refusal branch for a bare `probe:` section under an inject workflow
minors.detail: In `_check_raw_sections` (experimental_settings/schema.py, ~line 509), the generic per-section loop already rejects a top-level `probe:` key with "probe: no stage of this file's workflow reads this section" for any workflow lacking a `train` stage (since `probe` isn't in `_yaml_allowed_sections` there) -- which is every inject-workflow setting file that exists in this repo (inject.yaml's workflow is [inject, score]). The more specific inject-only check right below it, `if "probe" in d: raise SchemaError("probe: a setting whose workflow contains inject may not state a probe section")`, is therefore dead code for every realistic file: it would only ever fire for a hypothetical workflow that names both `inject` and `train` at once. Not a functional bug -- the acceptance test only checks that the message names the field `probe`, which both branches satisfy -- but the second message is effectively unreachable and should be removed or the ordering reconsidered.

minors.title: A couple of unused local variables
minors.detail: `_apply_fields` binds `f = next(f for f in dc_fields(cls) if f.name == key)` (~line 467) and never reads `f` afterward (the existence check it seemingly performs is already covered by the `key not in names` check two lines above). The override-application loop in `_merge_one` (~line 550) unpacks `field_name` from `dotted.partition(".")` and never uses it. Both are harmless dead assignments, cosmetic only.

concerns: D2's last print statement expects `S.key('train', c2) != S.key('train', c)` to be True, but got False. Root cause: the script never snapshots `S.key('train', c)` before editing trainer.py (unlike the probe_eval sub-test one line above it, which does snapshot `k0` first) -- key() correctly reads VERSION live from disk every call (per 3.3's explicit design), so two structurally-identical settings queried after the same edit necessarily key alike. I reproduced the probe_eval-style before/after snapshot pattern for trainer.py and got the ticket's expected 'True True', confirming the schema's VERSION-folding is correct and the D2 script itself has the bug. Documented in full in the report per spec.md section 7.

concerns: A0b's literal acceptance command crashes with AttributeError under system python3's dataclasses.py (_is_type does an unchecked sys.modules.get(cls.__module__).__dict__): this is a genuine CPython stdlib limitation that fires for ANY @dataclass with `from __future__ import annotations` loaded via module_from_spec+exec_module without first registering the module in sys.modules (importlib's own documented usage does register it first; the ticket's command does not). Reproduced with a two-line unrelated dataclass, and confirmed present under all three of system python3 (3.10.12), probe-env (3.11.15) and appworld venv (3.12.13). Both @dataclass (contracts 4.1) and `from __future__ import annotations` (spec.md section 5) are mandatory, so there is no code-level fix available; a corrected loader script (adding `sys.modules[name] = m` before exec_module) does print the expected `1 StepObservation`.

B6's second python block (computing appworld_at_module_level) crashes with AttributeError('Import' object has no attribute 'module'): its list comprehension unconditionally accesses `.module`, which only ast.ImportFrom nodes have, not plain ast.Import nodes (`import os`, `import re`, etc.) — a script bug that would hit any file using ordinary `import x` statements, including already-merged files like data/task_record.py and jobs/registry.py. Restyling appworld.py's imports into from-X-import-Y form solely to dodge this felt like gaming a broken check rather than a real fix, so I left normal import style and verified the intended property (no module-level `appworld` import) with a corrected diagnostic script, which prints appworld_at_module_level False.
Recommend both acceptance-script defects (A0b, B6) get fixed in the ticket file before wave 6, since run.py selfcheck may rely on similar patterns.

Two judgment calls with no acceptance coverage, documented in the report's Decisions section: (1) open_env's combined single ValueError naming every missing method+attribute together rather than two separate refusals; (2) the exact bracket/quote-depth scan used to decide when build_call must quote a value ('_bare_safe'), validated only indirectly via B3's four cases and B4's 4040/4040 real-corpus round-trip, not by an acceptance case naming the exact rule.
